payload.title: The system_one.py module docstring calls enabled: false the seed, but the shipped aria-config/system-one-questions.json has carried enabled: true since 2026-10-03, so a reader is told that no call is made while every shadow decision point asks the external Jev service, and the docstring never names the decision (ADR-0027) that turned it on
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/system_one.py:5-8 (enabled: false, the seed, means no call and no row)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/system_one.py:536-537 (ask returns system_one_disabled only when the registry is not enabled; with the shipped value it proceeds to the call)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/system_one.py:12-32 (the egress rule is stated here, but the docstring does not say the shipped state is on and holds no reference to ADR-0027)
docs/recommendations/architectural-arbiter/2026-10-03-adr-0027-system-one-jev-egress.md (the egress policy under which commit 1818d28af turned System One on in shadow)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md document it (tier 4) where the first reader looks: a docstring that states a default the shipped file contradicts is a false statement of the module's own behaviour
payload.notes: Commit 1818d28af (2026-10-03, turn System One on in shadow, under ADR-0027's egress policy) flipped the shipped value on purpose and left the docstring written for the seed. A reader changing a decision point, or checking what leaves the host, reads that false means no call and concludes the shipped state is quiet; in fact a cycle sends typed questions built from public references to Jev, an external service, in shadow. The egress rules that bound it are in the docstring body, but the one sentence that states the shipped value is wrong and the deciding ADR is not cited. Close condition: The docstring states that the shipped registry is enabled: true and cites ADR-0027, and a test reads aria-config/system-one-questions.json and asserts that the module docstring names the same enabled value, so the two cannot drift again. Verified at origin/main db10640f6.
